facts.text: Fort Montaigne d'Aigle, later called Eagle Hills Fort, was founded by Canadians nine miles below the confluence of the North Saskatchewan and Battle Rivers in 1778.
The Battlefords area hosted Cree, Blackfeet, and Assiniboine First Nations, all vying for local resources long before European arrival.
Battleford, founded in 1875 on the south side of the North Saskatchewan River, became the capital of the North-West Territories from 1876 to 1883.
Armoury Brewing, a local microbrewery, occupies a restored 1913 armoury, turning historic military space into craft beer on the riverbank.
North Battleford houses the Saskatchewan Western Development Museum branch, showcasing the province's agricultural history in a pioneer village setting.
The North Battleford Energy Centre, a natural gas-fired plant owned by Northland Power, has been supplying electricity since 2013.
